keywords: Organic Chemistry 2.Inorganic Chemistry 3.Physical Chemistry 4.Analytical Chemistry 5.Artes Liberales
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn what chemistry is and why it is indispensable to society through lectures and practical training. In addition, participants will obtain a deep understanding of chemistry from the viewpoint of cultural, historical, and social perspectives. The course also considers the connections between chemistry and various fields such as engineering, architecture, psychology, and information technology.
advice: Through lectures and experiments, participants will learn about ancient Mesopotamian culture, classical ancient Greek and Roman culture, medieval European and Islamic culture, and the process of the establishment of chemistry in modern times. In this course, students do not learn the history of chemistry as knowledge, but rather through hands-on experience in dye synthesis, glass synthesis, battery production, alloy production, etc., as well as a background in chemistry. All participants should be sure to work on the assigned preparation work for the laboratory experiences and discussions. The grade evaluation is based on reports and oral examinations.
books: [Reference books in English] The Demon-Haunted World: Science as a Candle in the Dark, Carl Segan, Ballantine Books(1997) [Reserved/Reference books in Japanese] 物質理論の探求[岩波書店]、百万人の化学史[アグネ承風社]、キリスト教文化の常識[講談社]、テクノクラートの勃興[筑摩書房],化学史への招待[オーム社]、日本の近代科学史[朝倉書店]
requiredKnowledge: Participants should have taken "Fundamentals of Chemistry" and "Fundamentals of Physics" in high school. No prior experience with chemistry experiments is required.

activityGoals.body: You will be able to describe how chemistry plays a role in society.
You will be able to explain various phenomena in terms of chemistry.
You will be able to perform basic chemistry experiments.

achievementLevels.ideal: After this course, you will be able to: - Explain the origin and development of chemistry and the role of chemistry in society. -Explain the relationship between chemistry and other fields, such as engineering, architecture, and information technology, with described examples. - Perform and explain historical chemistry experiments.

lessons.content: Introduction to the History of Chemistry - Chemistry in Antiquity, Classical Antiquity, the Middle Ages, and Modern Times. - The role of chemistry in society. - Preparation for laboratory hands-on.
lessons.assignments: Research examples of the use of "chemistry" in your major and summarize them on an A4 sheet.

lessons.content: Physical Chemistry in the Middle Ages - Distillation of alcohol - Extraction with Alcohol
